title: Microsoft 365 admin center: pay for Copilot Chat from prepaid capacity packs alone
summary: The standalone prepaid configuration, licensing, administrator roles and control operations are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge Microsoft's differing overage-enforcement descriptions, name the API request properties and align the checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes using a prepaid capacity pack as the sole billing method for supported Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: Use a prepaid capacity pack as the sole billing method for supported Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: The roadmap says policy users' usage is deducted exclusively from prepaid credits with no pay-as-you-go charges.
claims.quote: Admins can configure billing policies with prepaid capacity such that usage for users in the policy is deducted exclusively from prepaid capacity credits, with no pay as you go charges.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: With a standalone policy, covered users consume credits only from the prepaid pool.
claims.quote: If you use a Prepaid Capacity pack by itself (without pairing it with a pay-as-you-go billing policy), users covered by the credit policy consume credits only from the prepaid credit pool.

claims.claim: A standalone Copilot credit policy requires no Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Use this option if you want to use Prepaid Capacity pack credits without setting up pay-as-you-go billing. No Azure subscription is required.

claims.claim: A standalone Copilot credit policy does not require a pay-as-you-go billing policy.
claims.quote: You can create a Copilot credit policy to use capacity pack credits by themselves, without requiring a pay-as-you-go billing policy or an Azure subscription.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot Chat is unavailable for standalone-policy users when prepaid credits are exhausted until the next monthly period.
claims.quote: When prepaid credits are exhausted, Copilot Chat is unavailable for those users until credits replenish at the next billing cycle.
claims.fix: Keep the standalone-policy statement, but add: 'The Copilot Studio billing rates page separately describes enforcement for custom agents under prepaid capacity at 125% of tenant capacity, with possible exemptions for Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users; it does not reconcile that description with the standalone Copilot Chat policy description.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management#overage-enforcement.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The credit policy scope control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go services > Microsoft Copilot Chat > Copilot credit policies > Create a Copilot credit policy > Scope.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Billing & usage. ... Select the Pay-as-you-go services tab, and then select Microsoft Copilot Chat. ... In the Copilot credit policies section, select Create a Copilot credit policy. ... Under Scope, select the user groups

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: No API for creating or editing the classic Copilot credit policies is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot credit policies API Microsoft Graph create update prepaid capacity'; 'Copilot credit policy API PowerShell Graph prepaid'. Opened capacity-packs and Cost Management API overview; results document spending policies and environment allocations, not classic credit-policy operations.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The overage billing Connection status control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go services > Microsoft Copilot Chat > billing policy > Connection status.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Billing & usage. ... Select the Pay-as-you-go services tab ... Microsoft Copilot Chat ... Find the billing policy name, then switch the Connection status toggle to Connected.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for connecting the classic Copilot Chat overage billing policy is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph connect disconnect pay-as-you-go billing policy Copilot Chat connection status API'; 'billing policy Copilot Chat API connect Power Platform'. Opened commerce setup, capacity-packs and Cost Management API overview; none documents the classic connection toggle operation.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Tenant capacity draw is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio > Summary > Capacity summary > Prepaid Capacity > License type > Manage capacity > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: select Licensing > Copilot Studio. ... On the Summary tab, under Capacity summary ... Prepaid Capacity card. In the License type column, select Manage capacity. ... Select the Microsoft Copilot Chat environment. ... Under Capacity overages ... Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: PUT /licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 sets the TenantPool enforcement rule for MCSMessages.
claims.quote: $apiVersion = "2024-10-01" ... entitlementId = "MCSMessages" ... @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false } ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"
claims.fix: Keep the call. Replace the first sentence of controls[2].note with: 'The request body sets allocatedEntitlements[].enforcementRules with ruleType TenantPool and enabled true or false for entitlementId MCSMessages.' The fields are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/programmability-tutorial-manage-copilot-credit-allocations.

claims.claim: Draw from the available capacity in my tenant permits an environment to use unallocated tenant prepaid capacity after exhausting its allocation.
claims.quote: Under Capacity overages, choose how an environment can continue using Copilot Credits after it exhausts its allocated capacity: ... Select Draw from the available capacity in my tenant to let the environment use unallocated prepaid capacity from the tenant pool.

claims.claim: Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan permits continued usage through the selected billing plan.
claims.quote: Select Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan to let the environment continue usage through the selected billing plan.

claims.claim: The Capacity overages pane offers both tenant capacity draw and pay-as-you-go billing, and administrators can select one or both.
claims.quote: Under Capacity overages, select the options for what happens when capacity reaches zero. You can choose one or both of the following options: ... Draw from the available capacity in my tenant. ... Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan.

claims.claim: With no overage source enabled, an environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits.
claims.quote: If no overage source is enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits. Experiences that require credits can stop working after that allocation is exhausted.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The capacity management pane provides Overage notification settings for nearing capacity usage.
claims.quote: Under Overage notification, select the Send notification when nearing capacity usage checkbox, and then select a percentage value from the drop-down list.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Power Platform admin center's Copilot Studio licensing Summary tab reports total credits consumed and credits remaining.
claims.quote: go to Licensing > Copilot Studio. On the Summary tab, the Capacity summary section reflects Prepaid Capacity pack usage, shows how many credits were consumed in total, and shows how many remain available for the current period.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Cost Management monitoring page documents prepaid capacity consumption by Microsoft 365 and Power Platform services.
claims.quote: Prepaid Capacity pack credits usage (if applicable). Select the card to view details of Prepaid Capacity pack consumption by service. The flyout shows credits consumed by Microsoft 365 services and Power Platform services

claims.where: Governance controls: commerce setup entry point
claims.claim: The commerce setup page gives Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage as the entry point for Connection status in Manage billing policy connections.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost management . In the banner at the top of the dashboard, select Classic Billing & usage. ... select the Pay-as-you-go tab. ... Select the service ... In the Manage billing policy connections side panel ... select the Connection status toggle
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'The commerce setup page gives a different route: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go > service > Manage billing policy connections > billing policy > Connection status.' Keep the existing setup-page citation.

claims.claim: An environment group rule governing tenant capacity draw causes individual environment updates to be rejected with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: If a published environment group rule governs Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, you can't override the setting for an individual environment. Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: The allocation tutorial documents the TenantPool option, not the pay-as-you-go option in the capacity pane.
claims.quote: Searched: 'billing policy Copilot Chat API connect Power Platform'. Read the entire manage-copilot-credit-allocations tutorial, including UI steps and all code tabs: TenantPool is documented; Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan and a corresponding enforcement rule are not.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends roles with the fewest permissions.
claims.quote: Microsoft recommends that you use roles with the fewest permissions. Using roles with the fewest permissions helps improve security for your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Global Administrator as highly privileged and recommends limiting it to emergency scenarios where an existing role cannot be used.
claims.quote: Global Administrator is a highly privileged role that should be limited to emergency scenarios when you can't use an existing role.

claims.claim: The capacity packs page links to Copilot Studio Billing rates and management for the credit rates.
claims.quote: For more information about the billing rates for credits, see Billing rates and management - Microsoft Copilot Studio | Microsoft Learn.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe the Copilot credit policy as granting access to organizational data.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot credit policy data access permissions'. Read capacity-packs in full and returned Microsoft privacy excerpt: the policy is described as connecting credits to users; data access is described through underlying user permissions, not the credit policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Scoped standalone capacity supports departmental consumption from a shared prepaid pool without pay-as-you-go overage.
claims.quote: This feature enables departmental billing scenarios, allowing organizations to scope Copilot usage to defined teams and manage consumption from a shared pool of prepaid credits.

claims.claim: Learn documents prepaid capacity packs as a billing method for spending policies in Copilot cost management.
claims.quote: You can choose to apply Prepaid Capacity packs at the individual spending policy level in the Review billing method step.

claims.where: Open questions: spending policies; Cost and licensing: What happens at the limit
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends enabling pay-as-you-go to maintain service when prepaid capacity credits run out.
claims.quote: Enable a pay-as-you-go meter to ensure your services continue once Prepaid Capacity pack credits are exhausted.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: The checklist directs administrators to allocate capacity, monitor consumed and remaining credits and set Overage notification without corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: The allocation amount, monitoring and overage notification steps ... are not mapped as rows in the controls table. ... Monitor credits consumed and remaining ... Set the Overage notification
claims.fix: Replace the At rollout allocation bullet with 'Review Draw from the available capacity in my tenant in the Power Platform admin center (row 3).' Remove the After rollout bullets directing readers to monitor consumed and remaining credits and set Overage notification, because these controls have no table rows. Do not add rows.
